title: Volatility expansion
description: Short-window average true range divided by long-window average true range is at least expansion_ratio_min, and that condition has held for at least min_bars_expanded consecutive bars.
thesis: Realised volatility rising against its own longer-window baseline marks the transition out of balance. The ratio of two average true ranges over the same series is a scale-free statement of that transition.

required_hermes_fields.purpose: Average true range over short_atr_period bars.
Average true range over long_atr_period bars, forming the baseline.

parameters.name: short_atr_period
parameters.description: Lookback of the short-window average true range, in bars of the evaluated timeframe.

parameters.name: long_atr_period
parameters.description: Lookback of the baseline average true range, in bars of the evaluated timeframe. Must exceed short_atr_period for the ratio to express expansion rather than noise.

parameters.name: expansion_ratio_min
parameters.description: Minimum value of atr.short divided by atr.long for the bar to count as expanded. A value of 1.0 means the short window merely matches its baseline.

parameters.name: min_bars_expanded
parameters.description: Number of consecutive bars, ending at the evaluated bar, on which the ratio condition must hold.

direction_semantics.direction_rule: Volatility expansion carries no directional content: it states that the market is moving further per bar, not which way. The strategy always emits NEUTRAL, and a chain that needs a direction must take it from another input.

fields.name: matched
fields.description: True when the ratio condition has held for min_bars_expanded consecutive bars.

fields.name: expansion_ratio
fields.description: atr.short divided by atr.long on the evaluated bar.

fields.name: bars_expanded
fields.description: Consecutive bars ending at the evaluated bar on which the ratio condition held.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: The observed ratio, its threshold, the consecutive-bar count and whether each held.

deterministic_test_cases.description: Short ATR 12.0 against a baseline of 6.0 gives a ratio of 2.0, clearing the 1.5 threshold on one bar.
Short ATR 7.0 against a baseline of 6.0 gives a ratio of 7 divided by 6, below the 1.5 threshold.
The ratio clears the threshold on the evaluated bar only, but min_bars_expanded requires three consecutive bars.

provenance.source_reference: PID.md line 55 — volatility expansion, named as a canonical atomic strategy for HSA v1.
provenance.notes: Architect-set defaults. This entry is deliberately directionless and is the catalogue's worked example of an atomic strategy that emits NEUTRAL only; a chain composing it must take direction from a different input.
